newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended the week higher in trading described by dealers as listless.
Volumes were low, with activity concentrated only in a few issues.
Spread to Bunds narrows on short and long end. "There was quite a bit of chopping and changing between Sept 02s and Sept 01s, and reasonable activity in the benchmark 06," one dealer said.
He added there was a reasonably large seller in 6.25 July 1998s, but other dealers could not confirm this.

On Thursday, the short-end was somewhat under pressure, with the Sept 6.25 1998 closing down 0.05 points, which was said to be due to rumours of a likely hike in the special advances rate. The Dutch central bank held rates steady yesterday.
"I noticed no significant impact (of this) today," the dealer said.
Other dealers said rates would have to be raised sooner or later, but added short end-bonds were unaffected by this. Dutch bonds were mainly tracking Bunds, dealers said.
"They were lagging behind Bunds a bit, but this can be made up for on Monday," one dealer said.
He said some parties may have been reducing their positions before the weekend, and will get back into the market next week.
